Notes on hand-off notes for anyone flying with an animal
What you should know comes first
Hand-off notes for animal travel

Aurelia Skyways wants the hand-off to be smooth, clear, and calm. If you are flying with a pet, keep your note brief and practical so the crew can act fast and avoid mix-ups.

Put the basics up front: the animal's normal name, the carrier or crate it is using, and anything the team needs to do at the gate. If your pet is sensitive to noise, stress, or handling, say so in plain language. The Companion Animal Travel Desk can use those notes to support a better hand-off at the skyport.

For rabbits, <<FACT F064>> Keep the note focused on safety and comfort, and make sure the crate is secure, clean, and easy to move.

For small dog travel, <<FACT F074>> Also add any feeding or medication instructions the crew should know, but keep it short. The clearest notes avoid long stories and stick to what matters right now.

If another traveler is helping with the hand-off, make sure everyone gives the same details. Mixed messages slow things down and can create stress for the animal. The best notes are simple, calm, and easy to verify at the counter or gate.

If something in your plan changes, tell the Companion Animal Travel Desk as soon as you can so the team can review it step by step. For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk directly.
